ov: Venomous reef fish of the coastal Indo-Pacific, grey and mottled so they look like a stone or a lump of coral. Needle-like spines on the back carry the strongest venom of any known fish, and most stings happen when people step on one.

why.dg: The most venomous fish known: stings are extremely painful and can kill if untreated. Hot water and antivenom are the main treatments.
why.et: A delicacy in parts of Asia once the venomous spines are removed; heat breaks the venom down.

len: Usually about 27 cm; up to 40 cm (reef stonefish)
rg: Shallow tropical waters of the Indian and western Pacific Oceans, from the Red Sea and East Africa to Australia, southern Japan and French Polynesia.
df: Small fish, shrimps and other crustaceans, caught as they pass while it sits motionless on the reef.
fx: It can survive out of water for up to 24 hours, so stings can happen on the beach.
Its skin has no scales, only warts.
